survey.readings: Axis 15.3 degrees clockwise from east. Hall: long walls pleated in 1 m folds (BAG ring alternates 6.6/7.3 m off the axis), pointed west end, slanted plain east gable; eaves about 14.6-15 m, low ridge 17.6 m. Low ring 3.6-5 m round the west end and the south side. Tower at the north-east corner, top sloping from 34.5 m (south) to 45.5 m (north). Parish wing to the south-east, 8.5 m, and a 6.9 m link.

east gable: 43-window diamond lattice, three doors, name board, pier, tower; facade compare
south long wall over the ring: a slit in every inward fold up to the tower (eight), the plain east end and pier, wing

facadeRhythm.long walls: Brick pleated in 1 m folds from the ground to the crown; each fold's top rises above the low roof, the outer folds 1.5 m higher than the inner, so the crown reads as a zigzag. South wall: a tall narrow glass slit in every inward fold from the west corner to the tower (eight, RCE 20357073), above the low ring. North wall: taken as the same (no ring; slits from 2 m), inferred.
facadeRhythm.west point: The pleated walls meet in a point; the crown rises towards the middle (it follows the roof's section); three tall slits in the central inward folds (photo 001).
facadeRhythm.east gable: Plain brick gable: a diamond lattice of 43 small square windows (nine staggered columns, 4-5-5-5-5-5-5-5-4) centred about 10.8 m up; three entrance doors at the head of a stair under a name board; a plain brick pier rising behind the south corner; the tower beside it to the north (RCE 20357069).
facadeRhythm.low ring: Single storey round the west point and along the south: concrete posts, glazing, wooden blinds (some panels ochre), a thin concrete fascia and a dark roof.
facadeRhythm.tower: Brick slab, the top a single slope rising to the north from 34.5 to 45.5 m, zinc-clad with a projecting lip; a belfry opening with a cross beside it on the two broad faces.
facadeRhythm.parish wing: Brick, two storeys, a band of windows on the upper floor (and the ground floor on the south end), flat roof.

colours.sampled: 2023 (1) (sun, south-west): brick in shade #6c4d4d, panels #66462d, posts #868380, ring roof #b5afa2; 001 (sun, west): brick lit #d3ac8e.
colours.chosen: brick #b07462 (salmon-red; #9a6452 rendered too dark against the sunlit photos), concrete posts and fascias #d6d0c4, ochre blinds #b98d52, roofing #5a5c5e, tower top zinc #9aa3ac, glass #2f363c.

decisions: Plan from BAG (pleats and all), heights from 3DBAG; the roof is a low gable from intent, the tower top a single plane, nothing from the 3DBAG meshes.
The hall outline runs clockwise in plan coordinates, so its outward normals are to the left of travel; the first build had the crowns and slits on the inside (caught on the facade elevation).

The south long wall's slits are not checked by the facade compare: the folds stand 33 degrees off the wall, and the orthographic elevation sees the slits too narrow to count. The east gable is checked instead (passes).
The north wall's slits and the parish wing's window bands are inferred from the south side and from distant views.
